# The mcpredomics package is a supervised learning method for interpretable
# multiclass classification of metagenomic data. This method is derived 
# from one of the genetic algorithm-based heuristics in the predomics package.
# More details: https://github.com/predomics/predomicspkg

# Introduction

The mcpredomics package is designed to extend predomics, which was initially developed for binary classification, in order to enable multiclass classification of the gut microbiome.

# Visualization Functions

The package includes a variety of general-purpose visualization functions to explore models, their performance metrics, and the underlying populations. These functions allow users to gain valuable insights into their data and models with ease.

The implemented functions include:

* Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking
* Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking_ova

To learn more about the functionality of each visualization tool, use the `??` command followed by the function name. For example, `??printy_mc` provides detailed information about the `printy_mc` function.


# Multiclass Predictions and Aggregation Methods

The package supports multiclass modeling using one-versus-all (OVA) and one-versus-one (OVO) approaches. Additionally, it provides multiple methods for aggregating predictions from these approaches, as well as tools for evaluating the aggregated models.
The available functions are:
Prediction: predictModel_ova, predictModel_ovo,
Aggregation: voting, maximization, maximization_ovo, Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking, votingova, Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking_ova
Evaluation: evaluateModel_aggregation, evaluateModels_aggregation.
Each function serves a unique role, whether it involves generating predictions, combining results, or assessing model performance. For more details, use the ?? command, such as ??predictModel_ova for the predictModel_ova function.

# Multiclass Algorithm Implementations

We have extended the terBeam and terga1 algorithms to handle multiclass problems, introducing a set of specialized functions for model generation, feature combination management, and evolution optimization. These tools are designed to create scalable and efficient multiclass models.
The implemented functions include:
terBeam_mc, terBeam_fit_mc
generateAllSingleFeatureModel_mc, generateAllCombinations_mc
countEachFeatureApperance_mc, getFeatures2Keep_mc
terga1_mc, terga1_mc_fit
evolve_mc
You can explore the purpose and functionality of each function using the ?? command. For example, ??terBeam_fit_mc will provide a detailed explanation of the terBeam_fit_mc function.

# Core Functionalities

To ensure flexibility and efficiency in training, testing, and validating multiclass models, we have implemented the following core functions:
fit_mc: Fits models to the provided dataset.
runClassifier_mc: Executes the classifier to generate predictions.
runCrossval_mc: Runs cross-validation to evaluate model performance.
These foundational functions make it easier to integrate multiclass workflows into your projects. For detailed information on any of these functions, use the ?? command, such as ??runClassifier_mc for the runClassifier_mc function.

## Dataset

We conducted experiments on several datasets. The first one comes from the MetaCardis project and consists of four enterotype groups: Bacteroidetes1, Bacteroidetes2, Prevotella, and Ruminococcus. To this end, we created an initial balanced dataset by randomly extracting the same number of samples from each group. We then used the original unbalanced dataset.

In addition, we integrated into our package the list predomics.inputs.ExperimentHubMulticlass, which contains about ten multiclass microbial datasets. In this study, we experimented with two of these datasets, namely:

A three-class dataset (Adenoma, Colorectal Cancer, Control) from the study by Qiang Feng et al.

A three-class dataset (T2D, IGT, and Control) from the study by Fredrik H. Karlsson.


### Balance the dataset Metacardis.

Here we present how to use the MetaCardis dataset with class balance. You simply need to uncomment the script to run it when needed.

```{r}
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Load data and required packages
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # mcpredomics provides the 'mc.input' demo object
 data("mc.input", package = "mcpredomics")
# 
# # 'createDataPartition' is provided by the 'caret' package
# # If you don't want to attach the package, replace the call by caret::createDataPartition(...)
 suppressPackageStartupMessages({
   if (!requireNamespace("caret", quietly = TRUE)) {
     stop("The 'caret' package is required for createDataPartition. Please install it: install.packages('caret')")
   }
 })
# 
# # 'filterNoSignal' is expected to be available (e.g., from predomics/mcpredomics)
# # Make sure the package exposing this function is loaded if needed.
# 
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Build response vector aligned with X
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
 set.seed(123)  # For reproducibility of any random steps above
 yvec <- mc.input$y$Enterotype[match(colnames(mc.input$X), rownames(mc.input$y))]
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Basic filtering on features
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # Remove features with all-zero column sums
 X_general <- mc.input$X[, colSums(mc.input$X) != 0]
# 
# # Remove no-signal features (threshold set to "auto")
 X_general <- filterNoSignal(X = X_general, side = 1, threshold = "auto", verbose = FALSE)
# 
# # Final working copies
 set.seed(42)  # Reproducibility for the balancing step
 y <- as.vector(yvec)
 X <- X_general
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Determine the target sample count per class
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # Minimum class size; we will sample this many instances from each class
 nombre_echantillons_par_classe <- min(table(y))
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Helper to balance classes while preserving original order
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # Balances the dataset by randomly sampling the same number of indices
# # from each class, then sorts indices to keep original column order.
 equilibrer_classes <- function(y, X, nombre_echantillons_par_classe, seed = 123) {
#   # Identify unique classes
   classes <- unique(y)
   indices_equilibres <- integer(0)
#   
#   # Sample an equal number of indices for each class
   for (classe in classes) {
     indices_classe <- which(y == classe)
     set.seed(seed)  # Keep reproducible sampling within each class
     indices_equilibres <- c(indices_equilibres, sample(indices_classe, nombre_echantillons_par_classe))
   }
#   
#   # Sort to preserve original order (important for aligned X columns)
   indices_equilibres <- sort(indices_equilibres)
   return(list(y = y[indices_equilibres], X = X[, indices_equilibres, drop = FALSE]))
 }
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Build the balanced dataset
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
 donnees_equilibrees <- equilibrer_classes(y, X, nombre_echantillons_par_classe)
 y_equilibre <- donnees_equilibrees$y
 X_equilibre <- donnees_equilibrees$X
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Train/test split (80/20) on the balanced data
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # Stratified split to keep class proportions in train/test
 set.seed(42)
 indices_division <- caret::createDataPartition(y_equilibre, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)
# 
# # Training split
 y <- as.vector(y_equilibre[indices_division])
 X <- X_equilibre[, indices_division, drop = FALSE]
# 
# # Test split
 y.test <- as.vector(y_equilibre[-indices_division])
 X.test <- X_equilibre[, -indices_division, drop = FALSE]
# 
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Quick sanity checks
# # --------------------------------------------
# 
# # Class distribution in training set
 print(table(y))
# 
# # Dimensions of training feature matrix
 print(dim(X))


```


### Original unbalanced dataset Metacardis

Please uncomment this code if needed.

```{r}
# # --------------------------------------------
# # Load the demo dataset provided in mcpredomics
# # --------------------------------------------
data("mc.input", package = "mcpredomics")

# --------------------------------------------
# Set a seed for reproducibility
# --------------------------------------------
set.seed(123)

# Extract the response vector (Enterotype labels)
# Ensure that columns of X and rows of y are properly aligned
yvec <- mc.input$y$Enterotype[match(colnames(mc.input$X), rownames(mc.input$y))]

# --------------------------------------------
# Filter features (columns)
# - Remove features with zero total abundance across all samples
# - Apply filterNoSignal to remove uninformative features
# --------------------------------------------
X_general <- mc.input$X[, colSums(mc.input$X) != 0]
X_general <- filterNoSignal(X = X_general, side = 1, threshold = "auto", verbose = FALSE)

# --------------------------------------------
# Prepare working dataset
# --------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)      # Reset seed for reproducibility
y <- as.vector(yvec)     # Response vector
X <- X_general           # Filtered feature matrix

# --------------------------------------------
# Create a stratified partition (80% training / 20% testing)
# The function createDataPartition from caret ensures class balance
# --------------------------------------------
set.seed(42)
indices_division <- createDataPartition(y, p = 0.8, list = FALSE)

# --------------------------------------------
# Split the data
# --------------------------------------------
# Training set
y <- as.vector(y[indices_division])
X <- X[, indices_division, drop = FALSE]

# Test set
y.test <- as.vector(y[-indices_division])
X.test <- X[, -indices_division, drop = FALSE]

# --------------------------------------------
# Quick checks:
# - Class distribution in the training set
# - Dimensions of the training feature matrix
# --------------------------------------------
table(y)
dim(X)

```

## Experiments

In this example, we rely on the multiclass terBeam heuristic combined with the semi-constrained factor and OVO binarization, as this configuration yielded the optimal results according to the analyses reported in the Analyse_Resultat_Finale file. 


```{r}
clf <- terBeam_mc(sparsity = c(4,9), 
                                max.nb.features = 1000,
                                seed = 1,
                                nCores = 1,
                                evalToFit = "accuracy_",
                                objective = "auc",
                                experiment.id = "terBeam_mc",
                                experiment.save = "nothing")
  
                      
 printy(clf)  
```



### Running experiment

Three different constraint factors are implemented in our multiclass Predomics framework:

- `unconstrained`,
- `fully_constrained`,
- `semi_constrained`.

In addition, several aggregation strategies are available for combining the binary OvA/OvO submodels into a final multiclass prediction, including:

- `maximization`,
- `voting`,
- `Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking`.

All these aggregation methods can be executed using both multiclass decomposition strategies:

- `One-vs-All (OvA)`,
- `One-vs-One (OvO)`.

In this study, we illustrate the proposed framework using the configuration that provided the best overall compromise between predictive performance and interpretability, namely:

- the `semi_constrained` constraint factor,
- the `Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking` aggregation strategy,
- and the `One-vs-One (OvO)` multiclass decomposition approach.

```{r running experiment, echo=TRUE, fig.width=5, warning=FALSE}
runit = TRUE
if(runit)
{
res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026 <- fit_mc(X = X, y = y, clf = clf,approch="ova", cross.validate = TRUE,aggregation_ = "Majority_Voting_with_Tie_Breaking", nfolds = 10, constraint_factor = "semi_constrained"); 
save(res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026 , clf, file ="res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026.rda", compression_level = 9)
}


```



### Family of Best Models (FBM)

A family of best models (FBM) is defined as the subset of models returned by the Predomics optimization process whose predictive performances remain statistically comparable to the best-performing model.

The selection threshold is computed using a significance interval assuming that model accuracy follows a binomial distribution (p < 0.05). 

This strategy allows the identification of multiple sparse and interpretable candidate models that achieve near-optimal predictive performance while potentially involving different combinations of microbial features.


```{r}
# =========================================================
# Load result object
# =========================================================

load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026.rda")

# =========================================================
# Convert model collection into a population of models
# =========================================================

pop <- modelCollectionToPopulation(
  res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026$classifier$models
)

# =========================================================
# Select the best family of models
# =========================================================

fbm <- selectBestPopulation(pop)

# =========================================================
# fbm now contains the best model family
# =========================================================
best.model <- fbm[[1]]
printy_mc(fbm)
```

### Construction of Annotated Heatmap Data

This step builds an annotated dataframe used to visualize the interpretability patterns of the selected multiclass Predomics model. 

The function extracts the variables selected in each OvO binary submodel, associates them with their coefficient signs, and links them to taxonomic annotations (species and phylum levels). 

The resulting dataframe is structured for downstream visualization using heatmaps, enabling the identification of discriminative microbial signatures across binary comparisons.



```{r}
mod_annot_imbalance_Semi_VTB_ovo <- build_model_annotation_heatmap_data(
  y = y,
  X = X,
  best_model = best.model,
  taxo_file = "taxo_hs_9_9_igc_1436_CAG_sup_500_gtdb_214_long.tsv",
  approach = "ovo"
)
```


### Heatmap Visualization of Selected Features Across OvO Submodels

The heatmap displays the distribution of selected microbial features across OvO binary submodels obtained from the multiclass Predomics framework.

Each row corresponds to an annotated microbial feature, while each column represents a binary OvO comparison. 

Tile intensity reflects feature importance or selection presence within a given submodel, whereas point colors indicate the direction of association derived from the model coefficients:
- red points correspond to features associated with Class A,
- blue points correspond to features associated with Class B.

Features are grouped according to their phylum-level taxonomy in order to facilitate biological interpretation and highlight taxonomic patterns shared across binary classifiers.

```{r fig.heigth= 12, fig.width=14}
ggplot(mod_annot_imbalance_Semi_VTB_ovo, aes(x = model, y = feature.annot)) +
  geom_tile(aes(fill = importance), color = "grey90", linewidth = 0.3) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = sign_label),
    size = 2.8,
    stroke = 0,
    shape = 16,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "MDA | CV"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sign",
    values = c(
      "Class A" = "firebrick1",
      "Class B" = "deepskyblue1"
    ),
    breaks = c("Class A", "Class B"),
    labels = c("Class A", "Class B"),
    drop = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  facet_grid(phylum ~ ., scales = "free", space = "free") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 9),
    strip.text.y = element_text(angle = 0),
    legend.position = "right"
  )
```



### Build performance metrics dataframe
# =========================================================
#
# Description:
# This step constructs a structured dataframe containing
# cross-validation performance metrics obtained from the
# multiclass Predomics framework.
#
# The dataframe includes:
# - Accuracy
# - Recall
# - Precision
# - F1-score
# - Estimated TP, FP, FN
# - Error rate
#
# for both:
# - training sets
# - test sets
#
# across all cross-validation folds.
#
# In addition, the dataframe stores experiment metadata:
# - dataset name
# - sparsity level
# - constraint configuration
# - aggregation strategy
# - binarisation strategy
# - learning approach
#
# This structure facilitates:
# - statistical analysis
# - visualization
# - comparison between methods
# - reproducibility of experiments
#
# Each experiment-specific dataframe was individually
# generated and saved in order to preserve the complete
# performance information associated with a given
# experimental configuration.
#
# This includes:
# - Predomics models
# - state-of-the-art (SOTA) approaches
# - multiple datasets
# - different constraint levels
# - several aggregation strategies
# - OvO and OvA binarisation schemes
#
# After generating all individual experiment dataframes,
# they were merged into a single comprehensive dataframe
# gathering the complete set of experimental results = (Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo)
#
# This global dataframe was subsequently used for:
# - statistical comparisons,
# - mixed-effects modeling,
# - global performance analyses,
# - visualization of experimental trends,
# - and interpretation of multiclass classification
#   performances across all evaluated methods.
#
# =========================================================

```{r}
predo_imbalance_semi_VTB_terbeam_df <- build_experiment_metrics(
  
  # =====================================================
  # Result object containing CV performance metrics
  # =====================================================
  res_obj = res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026,
  # =====================================================
  # Best sparsity level selected during optimization
  #
  # Here:
  # k_9 corresponds to the best model using
  # 9 selected variables/features
  # =====================================================
  k_name = "k_9",
  # =====================================================
  # Number of training instances

  # =====================================================
  # Number of test instances

  # Approximately 10% of the dataset
  # used during cross-validation testing
  # =====================================================
  total_instances_test = 72,
  # =====================================================
  # Aggregation strategy used to combine
  # binary submodel predictions
  # =====================================================
  method_name = "Voting_with_Tie_Breaking",
  # =====================================================
  # Total number of variables/features
  # present in the original dataset
  # =====================================================
  k_value = "3385",
  # =====================================================
  # Constraint level applied during
  # variable selection
  # =====================================================
  constraint_factor = "Semi_Constrained",
  # =====================================================
  # Dataset name
  # =====================================================
  dataset_name = "Imbalanced Enterotype",
  # =====================================================
  # Learning approach/model name
  # =====================================================
  approch_name = "Terbeam Predomics",
  # =====================================================
  # Multiclass binarisation strategy
  #
  # OVO = One-vs-One
  # =====================================================
  binarisation = "OVO",
  # =====================================================

  # =====================================================
  num_folds = 10
)
# =========================================================
# Display final dataframe
# =========================================================
print(predo_imbalance_semi_VTB_terbeam_df)
```

### Hyperparameter Analysis of the Predomics Framework
# =========================================================
#
# Description:
# This analysis investigates the impact of multiclass
# hyperparameter configurations within the Predomics
# framework using mixed-effects statistical modeling.
#
# The objective is to evaluate how:
# - learning approaches,
# - multiclass binarisation strategies,
# - and aggregation methods
#
# influence classification performances across multiple
# microbiome datasets.
#
# The analysis is based on the dataframe:
#
# Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo
#
# which corresponds to a comprehensive dataset obtained
# by merging all experiment-specific dataframes generated
# during the study.
#
# This global dataframe includes:
# - all Predomics experiments,
# - all state-of-the-art (SOTA) experiments,
# - all datasets,
# - all sparsity levels,
# - all constraint configurations,
# - all aggregation strategies,
# - and both OvO/OvA multiclass settings.
#
# Each row corresponds to a single fold-specific
# experimental result.
#
# The present analysis focuses exclusively on:
# - Predomics models,
# - test performances,
# - and valid multiclass configurations.
#
# Mixed-effects models are used to account for:
# - variability between datasets,
# - variability between CV folds,
# while estimating the global effects of:
# - approaches,
# - and binarisation strategies.
#

```{r warning=FALSE, fig.height=8, fig.width=10}

# =========================================================
# Load the complete experimental dataframe
# =========================================================

load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo.rda")
# =========================================================
# Filter dataframe for Predomics hyperparameter analysis
# =========================================================
#
# Keep only:
# - multiclass settings (exclude "NO")
# - Predomics approaches only
# - test performances only
#
# =========================================================
df_all <- Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo %>%
  filter(
    Binarisation != "NO",
    Approach != "Sota",
    Set == "Test"
  )
# =========================================================
# Dataset ordering
# =========================================================
#
# Define a consistent ordering of datasets for:
# - statistical reporting
# - plotting
# - reproducibility
#
# =========================================================
ds_order <- c(
  "Imbalanced Enterotype",
  "Balanced Enterotype",
  "Colorectal cancer",
  "T2D"
)
df_all$Dataset <- factor(
  df_all$Dataset,
  levels = ds_order
)
# =========================================================
# Mixed-effects model
# =========================================================
#
# Fixed effects:
# - Approach
# - Binarisation
# - Their interaction
#
# Random effects:
# - Dataset variability
# - Cross-validation fold variability
#
# =========================================================
m_all <- lmer(
  Accuracy ~ Approach * Binarisation +
    (1 | Dataset) +
    (1 | Fold),
  data = df_all
)
# =========================================================
# Estimated marginal means (EMMs)
# =========================================================
#
# Compute adjusted mean accuracies for each approach
# within each binarisation strategy.
#
# =========================================================

em_all <- emmeans(
  m_all,
  ~ Approach | Binarisation
)

em_all_df <- as.data.frame(em_all)
# =========================================================
# Pairwise comparisons between approaches
# =========================================================
#
# Compute pairwise contrasts and confidence intervals
# within each binarisation strategy.
#
# =========================================================
prs <- pairs(
  em_all,
  by = "Binarisation"
)
prs_df <- as.data.frame(prs)
prs_ci <- as.data.frame(
  confint(prs)
)
pairs_all <- merge(
  prs_df,
  prs_ci[, c(
    "contrast",
    "Binarisation",
    "lower.CL",
    "upper.CL"
  )],
  by = c("contrast", "Binarisation"),
  all.x = TRUE
)
# =========================================================
# Statistical significance annotations
# =========================================================
#
# Create:
# - significance categories
# - significance symbols
#
# =========================================================
pairs_all$p.value.cat <- ifelse(
  pairs_all$p.value < 0.05,
  "pvalue<0.05",
  "NS"
)
pairs_all$sig_symb <- cut(
  pairs_all$p.value,
  breaks = c(-Inf, 0.001, 0.01, 0.05, Inf),
  labels = c("***", "**", "*", "NS"),
  right = TRUE
)
cols_pv <- c(
  "pvalue<0.05" = muted("green"),
  "NS" = muted("red")
)
# =========================================================
# Compact letter display (CLD)
# =========================================================
#
# Groups approaches that are not significantly different.
#
# =========================================================
cld_tbl <- tryCatch(
  {
    as.data.frame(
      cld(
        em_all,
        by = "Binarisation"
      )
    )
  },
  error = function(e) {
    
    warning(
      paste(
        "CLD not computed.",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
    )
    NULL
  }
)
# =========================================================
# Merge CLD annotations with EMM dataframe
# =========================================================
if (!is.null(cld_tbl)) {
  
  cld_tbl$.group <- gsub(
    "\\s+",
    "",
    cld_tbl$.group
  )
  
  em_all_df <- em_all_df %>%
    left_join(
      cld_tbl %>%
        dplyr::select(
          Approach,
          Binarisation,
          .group
        ),
      by = c(
        "Approach",
        "Binarisation"
      )
    )
}
# =========================================================
# Define Predomics family categories
# =========================================================
#
# Used for plot coloring and interpretation.
#
# =========================================================
em_all_df <- em_all_df %>%
  mutate(
    Family = case_when(
      
      grepl(
        "^Terbeam",
        as.character(Approach)
      ) ~ "Predomics Terbeam",
      
      grepl(
        "^Terga1",
        as.character(Approach)
      ) ~ "Predomics Terga1",
      
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )
# =========================================================
# Define family colors
# =========================================================
col_family <- c(
  "Predomics Terbeam" = muted("blue"),
  "Predomics Terga1" = muted("red")
)

present_levels <- intersect(
  names(col_family),
  unique(em_all_df$Family)
)
# =========================================================
# Panel 1:
# Estimated marginal means + confidence intervals
# =========================================================
p1 <- ggplot(
  em_all_df,
  aes(
    x = Approach,
    y = emmean,
    colour = Family
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    size = 4,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .25,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  {
    if (!is.null(cld_tbl))
      geom_text(
        aes(label = .group),
        vjust = -0.8,
        size = 5,
        colour = "black",
        show.legend = FALSE
      )
    else NULL
  } +
  scale_color_manual(
    values = col_family,
    breaks = present_levels,
    labels = present_levels,
    na.translate = FALSE,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation
  ) +
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Estimated mean Accuracy (EMMs)",
    x = NULL,
    colour = NULL
  ) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 5,
      r = 5,
      b = 0,
      l = 5
    ),
    panel.spacing.y = unit(4, "pt")
  ) +
  
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  )
# =========================================================
# Panel 2:
# Pairwise contrasts + confidence intervals
# =========================================================
p2 <- ggplot(
  pairs_all,
  aes(
    x = contrast,
    y = estimate
  )
) +
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = p.value.cat),
    size = 5
  ) +
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      colour = p.value.cat,
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .25
  ) +
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sig_symb),
    nudge_y = 0.02,
    size = 5,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = cols_pv,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "Significance",
    labels = c(
      "pvalue<0.05" = "Significant (p < 0.05)",
      "NS" = "Not significant"
    )
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Contrast estimate (EMMs differences)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 0,
      r = 5,
      b = 5,
      l = 5
    )
  )

# =========================================================
# Assemble final figure
# =========================================================

fig_all <- p1 + p2 +
  plot_layout(
    nrow = 2,
    heights = c(1, 1)
  )
# =========================================================
# Display final figure
# =========================================================
print(fig_all)
```


### Hyperparameter Analysis of Predomics Constraint Factors
# =========================================================
#
# Description:
# This analysis evaluates the effect of the constraint factor
# on the classification performance of the multiclass
# Predomics framework.
#
# The constraint factor corresponds to the level of restriction
# imposed during the variable selection process.
#
# Three constraint configurations are compared:
# - Full constrained
# - Semi constrained
# - Unconstrained
#
# The objective is to assess whether these constraint levels
# significantly influence test accuracy across:
# - Predomics learning approaches,
# - multiclass binarisation strategies,
# - cross-validation folds,
# - and microbiome datasets.
#
# The analysis uses the global dataframe:
#
# Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo
#
# This dataframe was obtained by merging all individual
# experiment-specific dataframes generated during the study.
# It contains both Predomics and state-of-the-art (SOTA)
# results, but the present analysis focuses only on Predomics
# configurations.
#
# Mixed-effects modeling is used to account for:
# - dataset-level variability,
# - fold-level variability,
# while estimating the fixed effects of:
# - constraint factor,
# - binarisation strategy,
# - learning approach,
# - and their interactions.


```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=10, warning=FALSE}
# =========================================================
# Filter dataframe for Predomics constraint analysis
# =========================================================
#
# Keep only:
# - valid multiclass binarisation strategies
# - Predomics approaches
# - test-set performances
#
# =========================================================
df_all <- Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo |>
  filter(
    Binarisation != "NO",
    Approach %in% c(
      "Terbeam Predomics",
      "Terga1 Predomics"
    ),
    Set == "Test"
  )
# =========================================================
# Define dataset ordering
# =========================================================
#
# This ensures consistent ordering in reports and plots.
#
# =========================================================
ds_levels <- c(
  "Imbalanced Enterotype",
  "Balanced Enterotype",
  "Colorectal cancer",
  "T2D"
)
df_all$Dataset <- factor(
  df_all$Dataset,
  levels = ds_levels
)
# =========================================================
# Clean and order constraint factor levels
# =========================================================
#
# Internal labels are converted into readable labels
# for visualization and reporting.
#
# =========================================================
cf_levels <- c(
  "Full_Constrained",
  "Semi_Constrained",
  "Unconstrained"
)
cf_labels <- c(
  "Full constrained",
  "Semi constrained",
  "Unconstrained"
)
df_all$Constraint_factor <- factor(
  df_all$Constraint_factor,
  levels = cf_levels,
  labels = cf_labels
)
# =========================================================
# Define colors for constraint levels
# =========================================================
cf_cols <- c(
  "Full constrained" = muted("purple"),
  "Semi constrained" = muted("orange"),
  "Unconstrained"    = muted("blue")
)
# =========================================================
# Mixed-effects model
# =========================================================
#
# Fixed effects:
# - Constraint factor
# - Binarisation strategy
# - Predomics approach
# - All interactions between these factors
#
# Random effects:
# - Dataset
# - Cross-validation fold
#
# =========================================================
m_all <- lmer(
  Accuracy ~ Constraint_factor *
    Binarisation *
    Approach +
    (1 | Dataset) +
    (1 | Fold),
  data = df_all
)
# =========================================================
# Estimated marginal means
# =========================================================
#
# Estimate adjusted mean accuracy for each constraint level
# within each combination of:
# - binarisation strategy
# - Predomics approach
#
# =========================================================
em_cf <- emmeans(
  m_all,
  ~ Constraint_factor | Binarisation + Approach
)
em_cf_df <- as.data.frame(em_cf)
# =========================================================
# Compact letter display
# =========================================================
#
# Constraint levels sharing the same letter are not
# significantly different within the same binarisation
# and approach condition.
#
# =========================================================
cld_tbl <- tryCatch(
  {
    as.data.frame(
      cld(
        em_cf,
        by = c(
          "Binarisation",
          "Approach"
        )
      )
    )
  },
  error = function(e) {
    warning(
      paste(
        "CLD not computed.",
        conditionMessage(e)
      )
    )
    NULL
  }
)
# =========================================================
# Merge CLD letters with EMM dataframe
# =========================================================

if (!is.null(cld_tbl)) {
  
  cld_tbl$.group <- gsub(
    "\\s+",
    "",
    cld_tbl$.group
  )
  
  em_cf_df <- em_cf_df |>
    left_join(
      cld_tbl[, c(
        "Constraint_factor",
        "Binarisation",
        "Approach",
        ".group"
      )],
      by = c(
        "Constraint_factor",
        "Binarisation",
        "Approach"
      )
    )
}
# =========================================================
# Pairwise contrasts between constraint levels
# =========================================================
#
# Compare constraint configurations pairwise within each
# binarisation and Predomics approach condition.
#
# =========================================================

prs <- pairs(
  em_cf,
  by = c(
    "Binarisation",
    "Approach"
  )
)

prs_df <- as.data.frame(prs)

prs_ci <- as.data.frame(
  confint(prs)
)

pairs_all <- merge(
  prs_df,
  prs_ci[, c(
    "contrast",
    "Binarisation",
    "Approach",
    "lower.CL",
    "upper.CL"
  )],
  by = c(
    "contrast",
    "Binarisation",
    "Approach"
  ),
  all.x = TRUE
)
# =========================================================
# Define significance categories
# =========================================================

pairs_all$p.value.cat <- ifelse(
  pairs_all$p.value < 0.05,
  "pvalue<0.05",
  "NS"
)
pairs_all$sig_symb <- cut(
  pairs_all$p.value,
  breaks = c(
    -Inf,
    0.001,
    0.01,
    0.05,
    Inf
  ),
  labels = c(
    "***",
    "**",
    "*",
    "NS"
  ),
  right = TRUE
)
pv_cols <- c(
  "pvalue<0.05" = muted("green"),
  "NS" = muted("red")
)

# =========================================================
# Panel 1:
# Estimated marginal means by constraint factor
# =========================================================
#
# This panel displays adjusted mean test accuracy and
# 95% confidence intervals for each constraint level.
#
# =========================================================

p1 <- ggplot(
  em_cf_df,
  aes(
    x = Constraint_factor,
    y = emmean,
    colour = Constraint_factor
  )
) +
  
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .25
  ) +
  
  {
    if (!is.null(cld_tbl))
      
      geom_text(
        aes(label = .group),
        vjust = -0.8,
        size = 5,
        colour = "black",
        show.legend = FALSE
      )
    
    else NULL
  } +
  
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = cf_cols,
    name = NULL,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(
    position = "top"
  ) +
  
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation + Approach,
    switch = "x"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Estimated mean Accuracy (EMMs)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 0,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.background.x = element_rect(
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey70"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 5,
      r = 5,
      b = 0,
      l = 5
    )
  ) +
  
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  )

# =========================================================
# Panel 2:
# Pairwise contrasts between constraint factors
# =========================================================
#
# This panel displays pairwise differences in estimated
# marginal means between constraint levels, with 95%
# confidence intervals and significance symbols.
#
# =========================================================

p2 <- ggplot(
  pairs_all,
  aes(
    x = contrast,
    y = estimate
  )
) +
  
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = p.value.cat),
    size = 5
  ) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      colour = p.value.cat,
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .25
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sig_symb),
    nudge_y = 0.02,
    size = 5,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation + Approach
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pv_cols,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "Significance",
    labels = c(
      "pvalue<0.05" = "Significant (p < 0.05)",
      "NS" = "Not significant"
    )
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Contrast estimate (EMMs differences)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 35,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.background.x = element_rect(
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey70"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 0,
      r = 5,
      b = 5,
      l = 5
    )
  )

# =========================================================
# Assemble final figure
# =========================================================

fig_cf <- p1 + p2 +
  plot_layout(
    nrow = 2,
    heights = c(1, 1)
  )

# =========================================================
# Display final figure
# =========================================================

print(fig_cf)
```


### Hyperparameter Analysis of Predomics Aggregation Methods
# =========================================================
#
# Description:
# This analysis evaluates the effect of aggregation methods
# on the classification performance of the multiclass
# Predomics framework.
#
# In the Predomics multiclass setting, several binary
# submodels are combined to produce a final multiclass
# prediction. This step compares the main aggregation
# strategies used for this purpose.
#
# The aggregation methods compared are:
# - Majority Voting
# - Voting with Tie-Breaking
# - Maximization
#
# The objective is to determine whether the choice of
# aggregation method significantly affects test accuracy
# across:
# - Predomics learning approaches,
# - multiclass binarisation strategies,
# - cross-validation folds,
# - and microbiome datasets.
#
# The analysis uses the global dataframe:
#
# Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo
#
# This dataframe was obtained by merging all individual
# experiment-specific dataframes generated during the study.
# It contains both Predomics and state-of-the-art (SOTA)
# results, but the present analysis focuses only on Predomics
# configurations.
#
# Mixed-effects modeling is used to account for:
# - dataset-level variability,
# - fold-level variability,
# while estimating the fixed effects of:
# - aggregation method,
# - binarisation strategy,
# - learning approach,
# - and their interactions.
#

```{r fig.width=14, fig.heigth = 8}

present_methods <- intersect(

# =========================================================

em_df <- as.data.frame(em_methods)

)


# =========================================================

if (!is.null(cld_tbl)) {

    "\\s+",

  em_df <- em_df |>

# =========================================================

prs_df <- as.data.frame(prs)

pairs_all <- merge(

  )],
  by = c(
    "contrast",

  ),

)


# =========================================================

pairs_all$p.value.cat <- ifelse(
  pairs_all$p.value < 0.05,

)

pairs_all$sig_symb <- cut(
  pairs_all$p.value,
  breaks = c(

# =========================================================

# =========================================================

p1 <- ggplot(
  em_df,
  aes(

  )
) +
  
  geom_point(size = 4) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      ymin = lower.CL,

    ),
    width = .25
  ) +
  
  {
    if (!is.null(cld_tbl))
      
      geom_text(

        size = 5,
        colour = "black",
        show.legend = FALSE
      )
    
    else NULL
  } +
  
  scale_colour_manual(
    values = pal,
    breaks = present_methods,
    name = NULL,
    drop = FALSE
  ) +
  
  scale_y_continuous(
    limits = c(0, 1),
    expand = expansion(
      mult = c(0, 0.08)
    )
  ) +
  
  scale_x_discrete(
    position = "top"
  ) +
  
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation + Approach,
    switch = "x"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Estimated mean Accuracy (EMMs)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "top",
    legend.direction = "horizontal",
    legend.box = "vertical",
    legend.margin = ggplot2::margin(b = 4),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 0,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.background.x = element_rect(
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey70"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 5,
      r = 5,
      b = 0,
      l = 5
    )
  ) +
  
  guides(
    colour = guide_legend(
      nrow = 1,
      byrow = TRUE
    )
  )


# =========================================================
# Panel 2:
# Pairwise contrasts between aggregation methods
# =========================================================
#
# This panel displays pairwise differences in estimated
# marginal means between aggregation methods, with 95%
# confidence intervals and significance symbols.
#
# =========================================================

p2 <- ggplot(
  pairs_all,
  aes(
    x = contrast,
    y = estimate
  )
) +
  
  geom_point(
    aes(colour = p.value.cat),
    size = 5
  ) +
  
  geom_errorbar(
    aes(
      colour = p.value.cat,
      ymin = lower.CL,
      ymax = upper.CL
    ),
    width = .25
  ) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(label = sig_symb),
    nudge_y = 0.02,
    size = 5,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  
  geom_hline(
    yintercept = 0,
    linetype = "dashed"
  ) +
  
  facet_nested(
    . ~ Binarisation + Approach
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    values = pv_cols,
    drop = FALSE,
    name = "Significance",
    labels = c(
      "pvalue<0.05" = "Significant (p < 0.05)",
      "NS" = "Not significant"
    )
  ) +
  
  coord_flip() +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    y = "Contrast estimate (EMMs differences)",
    x = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_bw(base_size = 18) +
  
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_blank(),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.text.x = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    strip.background.x = element_rect(
      fill = NA,
      colour = "grey70"
    ),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 0,
      r = 5,
      b = 5,
      l = 5
    )
  )


# =========================================================
# Assemble final figure
# =========================================================

fig_methods <- p1 + p2 +
  plot_layout(
    nrow = 2,
    heights = c(1, 1)
  )


# =========================================================
# Display final figure
# =========================================================

print(fig_methods)
```
