### Performance Analysis: Predomics vs State-of-the-Art Methods
# =========================================================
#
# Description:
# This analysis compares the test performance of selected
# Predomics configurations against state-of-the-art (SOTA)
# machine learning methods across multiple microbiome datasets.
#
# The analysis focuses on a fixed Predomics configuration:
# - Constraint factor: Semi_Constrained
# - Aggregation method: Voting_with_Tie_Breaking
# - Binarisation strategies: OVA and OVO
#
# Two Predomics learning approaches are evaluated separately:
# - Terbeam Predomics
# - Terga1 Predomics
#
# For each dataset, a mixed-effects model is fitted to compare
# Predomics variants with each SOTA method.
#
# The contrasts are explicitly defined as:
#
# Predomics - SOTA
#
# This means that positive contrast estimates indicate that
# the Predomics configuration has higher estimated accuracy
# than the corresponding SOTA method.
#
# The analysis uses the global dataframe:
#
# Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo
#
# This dataframe was obtained by merging all individual
# experiment-specific dataframes generated during the study,
# including both Predomics and SOTA experiments.
#
# For each dataset, the analysis produces:
# - Estimated marginal means of accuracy,
# - 95% confidence intervals,
# - pairwise contrasts between Predomics and SOTA methods,
# - statistical significance labels.
#


```{r fig.heigth=14, fig.width=16, warning=FALSE}
# One PDF figure is exported per dataset.
# =========================================================
# Define output directory
# =========================================================
#
# Figures are exported into the current working directory.
#
# =========================================================
out_dir <- getwd()
# =========================================================
# Define datasets to analyze
# =========================================================

datasets <- c(
  "Imbalanced Enterotype",
  "Balanced Enterotype",
  "Colorectal cancer",
  "T2D"
)
# =========================================================
# Identify SOTA methods present in the global dataframe
# =========================================================
sotamethods <- unique(
  Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo$Methods[
    Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo$Approach == "Sota"
  ]
)
# =========================================================
# Define significance colors
# =========================================================
cols_sig <- c(
  "pvalue<0.05" = muted("green"),
  "NS" = muted("red")
)
# =========================================================
# Main loop: one analysis and one PDF per dataset
# =========================================================
for (ds in datasets) {
  message("=== Dataset: ", ds, " ===")
  # =======================================================
  # Filter data for the current dataset
  # =======================================================
  #
  # Keep only:
  # - current dataset
  # - test-set performances
  # - OVA and OVO binarisation strategies
  # - SOTA methods
  # - Predomics methods using:
  #   * Semi_Constrained configuration
  #   * Voting_with_Tie_Breaking aggregation
  #
  # =======================================================
  ijdf <- Analysis_Dataset_Complet_Sota_vs_Predo %>%
    filter(
      Dataset == ds,
      Set == "Test",
      Binarisation %in% c("OVA", "OVO"),
      Binarisation != "NO"
    ) %>%
    filter(
      (Approach == "Sota") |
        (
          Approach %in% c(
            "Terbeam Predomics",
            "Terga1 Predomics"
          ) &
            Constraint_factor == "Semi_Constrained" &
            Methods == "Voting_with_Tie_Breaking"
        )
    ) %>%
    mutate(
      
      # Unified method labels for plotting
      
      Methods_plot = case_when(
        Approach == "Sota" ~ Methods,
        Approach == "Terbeam Predomics" ~
          "Predomics Terbeam SC VotingWTB",
        Approach == "Terga1 Predomics" ~
          "Predomics Terga1 SC VotingWTB",
        TRUE ~ Methods
      ),
      
      # Method family used for plot coloring
      
      Heuristic = case_when(
        Methods_plot == "Predomics Terbeam SC VotingWTB" ~ "Terbeam",
        Methods_plot == "Predomics Terga1 SC VotingWTB" ~ "Terga1",
        TRUE ~ "SOTA"
      )
    )
  # =======================================================
  # Safety check: ensure enough rows are available
  # =======================================================
  
  if (nrow(ijdf) < 5) {
    warning("Not enough rows for dataset: ", ds)
    next
  }
  # =======================================================
  # Prepare plotting factors
  # =======================================================
  
  ijdf$Methods_plot <- as.character(
    ijdf$Methods_plot
  )
  
  ijdf$Methods_plot <- factor(
    ijdf$Methods_plot
  )
  
  ijdf$Heuristic <- factor(
    ijdf$Heuristic,
    levels = c(
      "SOTA",
      "Terbeam",
      "Terga1"
    )
  )
  # =======================================================
  # Safety check: at least two methods are required
  # =======================================================
  
  if (nlevels(ijdf$Methods_plot) < 2) {
    warning(
      "Not enough Methods_plot levels for dataset: ",
      ds
    )
    next
  }
  # =======================================================
  # Mixed-effects model for the current dataset
  # =======================================================
  #
  # Fixed effects:
  # - Methods_plot
  # - Binarisation
  # - Their interaction
  #
  # Random effect:
  # - Cross-validation fold
  #
  # =======================================================
  
  m <- lmer(
    Accuracy ~ Methods_plot * Binarisation +
      (1 | Fold),
    data = ijdf
  )
  
  # =======================================================
  # Estimated marginal means
  # =======================================================
  #
  # Compute adjusted mean accuracy for each method within
  # each binarisation strategy.
  #
  # =======================================================
  
  em <- emmeans(
    m,
    ~ Methods_plot | Binarisation
  )
  
  em_df <- as.data.frame(em) %>%
    mutate(
      Heuristic = case_when(
        Methods_plot == "Predomics Terbeam SC VotingWTB" ~ "Terbeam",
        Methods_plot == "Predomics Terga1 SC VotingWTB" ~ "Terga1",
        TRUE ~ "SOTA"
      ),
      Heuristic = factor(
        Heuristic,
        levels = c(
          "SOTA",
          "Terbeam",
          "Terga1"
        )
      )
    )
  
  # =======================================================
  # Build Predomics-vs-SOTA contrasts
  # =======================================================
  #
  # Contrasts are defined as:
  #
  # Predomics - SOTA
  #
  # Therefore:
  # - positive estimate: Predomics > SOTA
  # - negative estimate: Predomics < SOTA
  #
  # =======================================================
  
  all_levels <- levels(
    ijdf$Methods_plot
  )
  
  pres_tbl <- ijdf %>%
    mutate(
      Methods_plot = factor(
        Methods_plot,
        levels = all_levels
      )
    ) %>%
    count(
      Binarisation,
      Methods_plot
    ) %>%
    tidyr::complete(
      Binarisation,
      Methods_plot,
      fill = list(n = 0)
    )
  
  # =======================================================
  # Helper function: check level presence
  # =======================================================
  
  is_present <- function(b, lev) {
    pres_tbl$n[
      pres_tbl$Binarisation == b &
        as.character(pres_tbl$Methods_plot) == lev
    ] > 0
  }
  
  # =======================================================
  # Helper function: construct one contrast vector
  # =======================================================
  
  make_one_contrast <- function(pred_name, sota_name) {
    
    v <- rep(
      0,
      length(all_levels)
    )
    
    names(v) <- all_levels
    
    v[pred_name] <- 1
    v[sota_name] <- -1
    
    v
  }
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Create all valid Predomics-vs-SOTA contrasts
  # =======================================================
  
  contrast_list <- list()
  
  bins <- sort(
    unique(
      as.character(ijdf$Binarisation)
    )
  )
  
  for (b in bins) {
    
    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Terbeam Predomics contrasts
    # -----------------------------------------------------
    
    pred_tb <- "Predomics Terbeam SC VotingWTB"
    
    if (
      pred_tb %in% all_levels &&
      is_present(b, pred_tb)
    ) {
      
      for (
        sota in setdiff(
          all_levels,
          c(
            pred_tb,
            "Predomics Terga1 SC VotingWTB"
          )
        )
      ) {
        
        if (is_present(b, sota)) {
          
          nm <- paste0(
            pred_tb,
            " - ",
            sota
          )
          
          contrast_list[[nm]] <-
            make_one_contrast(
              pred_tb,
              sota
            )
        }
      }
    }
    
    
    # -----------------------------------------------------
    # Terga1 Predomics contrasts
    # -----------------------------------------------------
    
    pred_tg <- "Predomics Terga1 SC VotingWTB"
    
    if (
      pred_tg %in% all_levels &&
      is_present(b, pred_tg)
    ) {
      
      for (
        sota in setdiff(
          all_levels,
          c(
            pred_tg,
            "Predomics Terbeam SC VotingWTB"
          )
        )
      ) {
        
        if (is_present(b, sota)) {
          
          nm <- paste0(
            pred_tg,
            " - ",
            sota
          )
          
          contrast_list[[nm]] <-
            make_one_contrast(
              pred_tg,
              sota
            )
        }
      }
    }
  }
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Safety check: ensure at least one contrast exists
  # =======================================================
  
  if (length(contrast_list) == 0) {
    warning(
      "No valid Predomics-vs-SOTA contrasts for dataset: ",
      ds
    )
    next
  }
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Apply contrasts within each binarisation strategy
  # =======================================================
  
  ct <- contrast(
    em,
    method = contrast_list,
    by = "Binarisation"
  )
  
  ct_df <- as.data.frame(ct)
  
  ct_ci <- as.data.frame(
    confint(ct)
  )
  
  pairs_all <- merge(
    ct_df,
    ct_ci[, c(
      "contrast",
      "Binarisation",
      "lower.CL",
      "upper.CL"
    )],
    by = c(
      "contrast",
      "Binarisation"
    ),
    all.x = TRUE
  ) %>%
    mutate(
      
      # Significance category
      
      p.value.cat = ifelse(
        p.value < 0.05,
        "pvalue<0.05",
        "NS"
      ),
      
      # Significance symbol
      
      sig_symb = cut(
        p.value,
        breaks = c(
          -Inf,
          0.001,
          0.01,
          0.05,
          Inf
        ),
        labels = c(
          "***",
          "**",
          "*",
          "NS"
        ),
        right = TRUE
      ),
      
      # Predomics variant involved in the contrast
      
      Predomics_variant = case_when(
        grepl("^Predomics Terbeam", contrast) ~ "Terbeam",
        grepl("^Predomics Terga1", contrast) ~ "Terga1",
        TRUE ~ "Other"
      )
    )
  
  pairs_all$Predomics_variant <- factor(
    pairs_all$Predomics_variant,
    levels = c(
      "Terbeam",
      "Terga1"
    )
  )
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Panel 1:
  # Estimated marginal means of accuracy
  # =======================================================
  
  p1 <- ggplot(
    em_df,
    aes(
      x = Methods_plot,
      y = emmean,
      colour = Heuristic
    )
  ) +
    
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = lower.CL,
        ymax = upper.CL
      ),
      width = .2
    ) +
    
    scale_x_discrete(
      position = "top"
    ) +
    
    facet_nested(
      . ~ Binarisation,
      switch = "x"
    ) +
    
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        ds,
        " – EMMs (Test only)"
      ),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Estimated mean Accuracy (EMMs)",
      colour = NULL
    ) +
    
    theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
    
    theme(
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 0
      ),
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold"
      ),
      legend.position = "top"
    )
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Panel 2:
  # Predomics-vs-SOTA contrasts
  # =======================================================
  
  p2 <- ggplot(
    pairs_all,
    aes(
      x = contrast,
      y = estimate,
      colour = p.value.cat
    )
  ) +
    
    geom_point(size = 3) +
    
    geom_errorbar(
      aes(
        ymin = lower.CL,
        ymax = upper.CL
      ),
      width = .2
    ) +
    
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sig_symb),
      nudge_y = 0.02,
      size = 4,
      show.legend = FALSE
    ) +
    
    geom_hline(
      yintercept = 0,
      linetype = "dashed"
    ) +
    
    facet_nested(
      Predomics_variant ~ Binarisation,
      scales = "free_y",
      space = "free_y"
    ) +
    
    scale_color_manual(
      values = cols_sig,
      name = NULL
    ) +
    
    coord_flip() +
    
    labs(
      title = paste0(
        ds,
        " – Contrasts (Test only): Predomics − each SOTA method"
      ),
      x = NULL,
      y = "Contrast estimate (95% CI)"
    ) +
    
    theme_bw(base_size = 16) +
    
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(
        face = "bold"
      )
    )
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Assemble final figure
  # =======================================================
  
  fig <- p1 / p2
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Display final figure
  # =======================================================
  
  print(fig)
  
  
  # =======================================================
  # Export PDF for the current dataset
  # =======================================================
  
  file_ds <- file.path(
    out_dir,
    paste0(
      "accuracy_sota_predomics_testonly_",
      gsub(
        "[^A-Za-z0-9]+",
        "_",
        tolower(ds)
      ),
      ".pdf"
    )
  )
  
  ggsave(
    filename = file_ds,
    plot = fig,
    width = 16,
    height = 12,
    units = "in"
  )
  
  message("Exported: ", file_ds)
}
```


## ============================================================
### Interpretability Analysis of the Best Predomics Models
## ============================================================
##
## Description:
## This section focuses on the biological interpretability of
## the best Predomics models obtained for the T2D dataset.
##
## The objects:
## - mda_complete.annot_full_constraint_T2D
## - mda_complete.annot_semi_constraint_T2D
## - mda_complete.annot_unconstraint_T2D
##
## correspond to annotated interpretability files generated
## from the best model selected under each experimental
## configuration.
##
## Each file contains the variables selected by the best model,
## their cross-validated MDA importance values, their coefficient
## signs, and their taxonomic annotations.
##
## These annotated files were obtained separately according to:
## - the constraint configuration,
## - the aggregation method,
## - the binarisation strategy,
## - the learning approach,
## - and the selected family of best models.
##
## In this analysis, the annotated results from the full,
## semi-constrained, and unconstrained configurations are merged
## into a single long-format dataframe.
##
## The resulting heatmap allows comparison of microbial features
## selected across constraint settings.
##
## In the figure:
## - tiles represent the MDA-based importance of each feature,
## - dots represent the sign of the coefficient,
## - rows correspond to annotated microbial species,
## - columns correspond to OvO binary submodels,
## - facets separate taxonomic phyla and constraint settings.
##
## This visualization helps identify which microbial signatures
## are stable, specific, or variable across Predomics constraint
## configurations.
##

```{r fig.width=14, fig.heigth = 12, warning=TRUE}
full_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mda_complete.annot_full_constraint_T2D.rda"
semi_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mda_complete.annot_semi_constraint_T2D.rda"
unco_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mda_complete.annot_unconstraint_T2D.rda"

stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(full_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(semi_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(unco_path)))

## ----------------------------
## 2) Load data and add source label
## ----------------------------
##
## Each loaded object is tagged with its corresponding
## constraint configuration in order to facilitate:
## - merging,
## - comparison,
## - and downstream visualization.
##
## The source variable is later used for:
## - facet organization,
## - interpretability comparison,
## - and constraint-specific analysis.
##
## ----------------------------------------------------

load(full_path)
mda_complete.annot_full_constraint_T2D$source <- "full-constraint"

load(semi_path)
mda_complete.annot_semi_constraint_T2D$source <- "semi-constraint"

load(unco_path)
mda_complete.annot_unconstraint_T2D$source <- "unconstraint"


## Merge all annotated interpretability results
## into a single long-format dataframe
##
## This unified dataframe allows:
## - direct comparison between constraint settings,
## - identification of shared microbial signatures,
## - and visualization of stable biomarkers.

alldf <- bind_rows(
  mda_complete.annot_full_constraint_T2D,
  mda_complete.annot_semi_constraint_T2D,
  mda_complete.annot_unconstraint_T2D
)


## ----------------------------
## 3) Parse taxonomy from the feature string
## ----------------------------
##
## Taxonomic information is extracted directly from the
## microbial feature identifiers.
##
## The parsing step retrieves:
## - phylum information,
## - species-level annotations.
##
## These annotations are used to:
## - biologically organize the heatmap,
## - improve interpretability,
## - and highlight taxonomic patterns.
##
## ----------------------------------------------------

split_feat <- strsplit(alldf$feature, "\\|")

# Extract phylum (2nd field)
# and species (7th field) when available

alldf$phylum  <- sapply(
  split_feat,
  function(x)
    if (length(x) >= 2) x[2]
    else NA_character_
)

alldf$species <- sapply(
  split_feat,
  function(x)
    if (length(x) >= 7) x[7]
    else NA_character_
)


## ----------------------------
## 4) Reshape importance and coefficient
## ----------------------------
##
## Convert data from wide format to long format in order
## to facilitate:
## - heatmap visualization,
## - merging of importance and coefficient information,
## - and ggplot compatibility.
##
## Importance values correspond to:
## - cross-validated MDA importance scores.
##
## Coefficients correspond to:
## - the direction of association of each microbial
##   variable within the binary OvO submodels.
##
## ----------------------------------------------------


# ----------------------------------------------------
# Importance matrix
# ----------------------------------------------------

alldf2 <- dcast(
  alldf,
  species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "importance"
)

# Missing values correspond to absent features
# in a given constraint configuration and are
# replaced by zero.

alldf2[is.na(alldf2)] <- 0

# Convert to long format

alldf2 <- melt(
  alldf2,
  id.vars = c("species", "phylum", "model"),
  variable.name = "source",
  value.name = "importance"
)


# ----------------------------------------------------
# Coefficient matrix
# ----------------------------------------------------

alldf3 <- dcast(
  alldf,
  species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "coefficient"
)

# Missing coefficients are replaced by zero

alldf3[is.na(alldf3)] <- 0

# Convert to long format

alldf3 <- melt(
  alldf3,
  id.vars = c("species", "phylum", "model"),
  variable.name = "source",
  value.name = "coefficient"
)


## ----------------------------
## 5) Merge importance and coefficient information
## ----------------------------
##
## Join importance scores and coefficient signs into
## a unified dataframe used for visualization.
##
## Coefficient signs indicate:
## - negative association (-1),
## - positive association (+1),
## - absence of feature contribution (0).
##
## Constraint configurations are converted into ordered
## factors to ensure consistent visualization ordering.
##
## ----------------------------------------------------

alldf23 <- left_join(
  alldf2,
  alldf3,
  by = c(
    "species",
    "phylum",
    "model",
    "source"
  )
)

alldf23$coefficient <- factor(
  alldf23$coefficient,
  levels = c(-1, 1, 0)
)

alldf23$source <- factor(
  alldf23$source,
  levels = c(
    "full-constraint",
    "semi-constraint",
    "unconstraint"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "full\nconstraint",
    "semi\nconstraint",
    "unconstraint"
  )
)


## ----------------------------
## 6) Heatmap visualization
## ----------------------------
##
## Heatmap representation of the microbial signatures
## selected by the best Predomics models.
##
## Interpretation:
##
## - Tiles:
##   represent MDA importance scores obtained during
##   cross-validation.
##
## - Dots:
##   represent the coefficient sign associated with
##   each microbial feature.
##
## - Red dots:
##   negative contribution.
##
## - Blue dots:
##   positive contribution.
##
## - White:
##   absence of contribution.
##
## The figure enables:
## - comparison of microbial signatures across
##   constraint configurations,
## - visualization of stable biomarkers,
## - and biological interpretation of multiclass
##   OvO Predomics models.
##
## ----------------------------------------------------

p_top <- ggplot(alldf23, aes(x = model, y = species)) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = importance),
    color = "grey90",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = coefficient),
    size = 3.8,
    stroke = 0,
    shape = 16,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "MDA | CV"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name   = "Sign",
    values = c(
      "firebrick1",
      "deepskyblue1",
      "white"
    ),
    breaks = c(-1, 1, 0),
    labels = c("-1", "1", ""),
    drop   = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    phylum ~ source,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 25,
      b = 10,
      l = 30
    ),
    strip.text.y = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

print(p_top)
save(
  alldf,
  alldf2,
  alldf3,
  alldf23,
  p_top,
  file = "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/T2D_interpretability_analysis_workspace.rda",
  compress = "xz"
)
```


### Interpretability Analysis of the Imbalanced Enterotype Dataset
## ============================================================
##
## Description:
## This section presents the interpretability analysis of the
## best multiclass Predomics models obtained for the
## Imbalanced Enterotype dataset.
##
## The analysis compares microbial signatures identified under
## three different constraint configurations:
## - full constrained,
## - semi-constrained,
## - unconstrained.
##
## The input files:
## - data_contraint1
## - data_semicontraint3
## - data_uncontraint2
##
## correspond to annotated interpretability outputs generated
## from the best-performing Predomics models selected during
## the multiclass optimization process.
##
## Each file contains:
## - microbial variables selected by the model,
## - cross-validated MDA importance scores,
## - coefficient signs,
## - taxonomic annotations,
## - and OvO multiclass submodel information.
##
## These annotated results were generated separately according
## to:
## - the constraint configuration,
## - the aggregation strategy,
## - the binarisation strategy,
## - the learning approach,
## - and the selected sparsity level.
##
## The objective of this analysis is to compare how microbial
## signatures vary across different Predomics constraint
## configurations.
##
## The three annotated datasets are merged into a single
## long-format dataframe in order to:
## - compare feature importance profiles,
## - identify stable microbial biomarkers,
## - visualize constraint-specific signatures,
## - and facilitate biological interpretation.
##
## In the heatmap:
##
## - Tiles:
##   represent MDA-based importance values obtained during
##   cross-validation.
##
## - Dots:
##   represent the coefficient sign associated with each
##   microbial variable.
##
## - Red dots:
##   indicate negative associations.
##
## - Blue dots:
##   indicate positive associations.
##
## - White:
##   indicates absence of contribution.
##
## The heatmap is organized according to:
## - microbial phylum,
## - constraint configuration,
## - and OvO multiclass submodels.
##
## This visualization facilitates the identification of:
## - robust microbial biomarkers,
## - taxonomic patterns,
## - and biologically interpretable multiclass signatures
## extracted by the Predomics framework.
##
## The final figure is exported in PDF format to ensure:
## - high graphical quality,
## - reproducibility,
## - and publication-ready rendering.
##
## ============================================================

```{r fig.width=18, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE}
## 1) File paths and validation
## ----------------------------

full_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/data_contraint1.rda"
semi_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/data_semicontraint3.rda"
unco_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/data_uncontraint2.rda"

stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(full_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(semi_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(unco_path)))


## ----------------------------
## 2) Load datasets
## ----------------------------

load(full_path)
load(semi_path)
load(unco_path)


## ----------------------------
## 3) Add source labels
## ----------------------------

data_contraint1$source <- "full-constraint"

data_semicontraint3$source <- "semi-constraint"

data_uncontraint2$source <- "unconstraint"


## ----------------------------
## 4) Merge datasets
## ----------------------------

alldf <- rbind(
  data_contraint1,
  data_semicontraint3,
  data_uncontraint2
)


## ----------------------------
## 5) Build species display labels
## ----------------------------

alldf$species <- ifelse(
  is.na(alldf$species),
  paste(alldf$feature, ":Unknown", sep = ""),
  paste(alldf$feature, alldf$species, sep = ":")
)


## ----------------------------
## 6) Importance reshaping
## ----------------------------

alldf2 <- reshape2::dcast(
  data = alldf,
  formula = species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "importance"
)

alldf2$`full-constraint` <- ifelse(
  is.na(alldf2$`full-constraint`),
  0,
  alldf2$`full-constraint`
)

alldf2$`semi-constraint` <- ifelse(
  is.na(alldf2$`semi-constraint`),
  0,
  alldf2$`semi-constraint`
)

alldf2$unconstraint <- ifelse(
  is.na(alldf2$unconstraint),
  0,
  alldf2$unconstraint
)

alldf2 <- reshape2::melt(alldf2)

colnames(alldf2) <- gsub(
  "variable",
  "source",
  colnames(alldf2)
)

colnames(alldf2) <- gsub(
  "value",
  "importance",
  colnames(alldf2)
)


## ----------------------------
## 7) Coefficient reshaping
## ----------------------------

alldf3 <- reshape2::dcast(
  data = alldf,
  formula = species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "coefficient"
)

alldf3 <- reshape2::melt(alldf3)

colnames(alldf3) <- gsub(
  "variable",
  "source",
  colnames(alldf3)
)

colnames(alldf3) <- gsub(
  "value",
  "coefficient",
  colnames(alldf3)
)

alldf3$coefficient <- ifelse(
  is.na(alldf3$coefficient),
  0,
  alldf3$coefficient
)

alldf3$coefficient <- factor(
  alldf3$coefficient,
  levels = c(-1, 1, 0)
)


## ----------------------------
## 8) Merge importance and coefficient
## ----------------------------

alldf23 <- cbind(
  alldf2,
  alldf3[, "coefficient", drop = FALSE]
)

alldf23$source <- factor(
  alldf23$source,
  levels = c(
    "full-constraint",
    "semi-constraint",
    "unconstraint"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "full\nconstraint",
    "semi\nconstraint",
    "unconstraint"
  )
)


## ----------------------------
## 9) Heatmap plot
## ----------------------------

p_top <- ggplot(alldf23, aes(x = model, y = species)) +
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = importance),
    color = "grey90",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  geom_point(
    aes(color = coefficient),
    size = 3.8,
    stroke = 0,
    shape = 16,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "MDA | CV"
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sign",
    values = c(
      "firebrick1",
      "deepskyblue1",
      "white"
    ),
    breaks = c(-1, 1, 0),
    labels = c("-1", "1", ""),
    drop = TRUE
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    phylum ~ source,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 60,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1,
      size = 14
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 20,
      b = 40,
      l = 20
    ),
    strip.text.y = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

print(p_top)


## ----------------------------
## 10) Save PDF figure
## ----------------------------

ggsave(
  filename = "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/enterotypes_heatmap.pdf",
  plot = p_top,
  device = "pdf",
  width = 16,
  height = 12
)
```


### Interpretability Analysis of the CRC Dataset
## ============================================================
##
## Description:
## This section presents the interpretability analysis of the
## best multiclass Predomics models obtained for the
## colorectal cancer (CRC) dataset.
##
## The analysis compares microbial signatures identified under
## three different constraint configurations:
## - full constrained,
## - semi-constrained,
## - unconstrained.
##
## The input files:
## - mod_annot_crc_full
## - mod_annot_crc_semi
## - mod_annot_crc_unco
##
## correspond to annotated interpretability outputs generated
## from the best-performing Predomics models selected during
## the multiclass optimization process.
##
## Each file contains:
## - microbial variables selected by the model,
## - cross-validated MDA importance scores,
## - coefficient signs,
## - taxonomic annotations,
## - and OvO multiclass submodel information.
##
## These annotated results were generated separately according
## to:
## - the constraint configuration,
## - the aggregation strategy,
## - the binarisation strategy,
## - the learning approach,
## - and the selected sparsity level.
##
## The objective is to compare how microbial signatures vary
## across Predomics constraint configurations in the CRC task.

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE}

full_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mod_annot_crc_full.rda"
semi_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mod_annot_crc_semi.rda"
unco_path <- "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/mod_annot_crc_unco.rda"

stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(full_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(semi_path)))
stopifnot(file.exists(path.expand(unco_path)))


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 2) Load annotated model objects
## ------------------------------------------------------------

load(full_path)
mod_annot_crc_full$source <- "full-constraint"

load(semi_path)
mod_annot_crc_semi$source <- "semi-constraint"

load(unco_path)
mod_annot_crc_unco$source <- "unconstraint"


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 3) Merge all constraint configurations
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf <- bind_rows(
  mod_annot_crc_full,
  mod_annot_crc_semi,
  mod_annot_crc_unco
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 4) Ensure feature column is character
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf$feature <- as.character(alldf$feature)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 5) Extract taxonomic information from feature string
## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
## Feature format example:
## k__Bacteria|p__Firmicutes|...|s__Species_name
##
## The parsing step extracts:
## - phylum-level annotation,
## - species-level annotation.
##
## These annotations are used to biologically organize
## the heatmap and facilitate interpretation.
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

split_feat <- strsplit(alldf$feature, "\\|")

alldf$phylum <- sapply(
  split_feat,
  function(x)
    if (length(x) >= 2) x[2]
    else NA_character_
)

alldf$species <- sapply(
  split_feat,
  function(x)
    if (length(x) >= 7) x[7]
    else NA_character_
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 6) Reshape importance values
## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
## MDA importance values are reshaped from wide to long
## format to allow ggplot-based heatmap visualization.
##
## Missing importance values correspond to features absent
## from a given constraint configuration and are replaced
## by zero.
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf2 <- dcast(
  alldf,
  species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "importance"
)

alldf2[is.na(alldf2)] <- 0

alldf2 <- melt(
  alldf2,
  id.vars = c(
    "species",
    "phylum",
    "model"
  ),
  variable.name = "source",
  value.name = "importance"
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 7) Reshape coefficient values
## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
## Coefficients are reshaped from wide to long format.
##
## The coefficient sign represents the direction of the
## contribution of each microbial feature within each OvO
## binary submodel.
##
## Missing coefficients are replaced by zero, indicating
## absence of contribution.
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf3 <- dcast(
  alldf,
  species + phylum + model ~ source,
  value.var = "coefficient"
)

alldf3[is.na(alldf3)] <- 0

alldf3 <- melt(
  alldf3,
  id.vars = c(
    "species",
    "phylum",
    "model"
  ),
  variable.name = "source",
  value.name = "coefficient"
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 8) Merge importance and coefficient information
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf23 <- left_join(
  alldf2,
  alldf3,
  by = c(
    "species",
    "phylum",
    "model",
    "source"
  )
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 9) Define factor levels for consistent ordering
## ------------------------------------------------------------

alldf23$coefficient <- factor(
  alldf23$coefficient,
  levels = c(-1, 1, 0)
)

alldf23$source <- factor(
  alldf23$source,
  levels = c(
    "full-constraint",
    "semi-constraint",
    "unconstraint"
  ),
  labels = c(
    "full\nconstraint",
    "semi\nconstraint",
    "unconstraint"
  )
)


## ------------------------------------------------------------
## 10) Heatmap visualization
## ------------------------------------------------------------
##
## Interpretation:
##
## - Tiles represent MDA importance scores.
## - Dots represent coefficient signs.
## - Red dots indicate negative contributions.
## - Blue dots indicate positive contributions.
## - White indicates absence of contribution.
##
## The heatmap is organized by:
## - microbial phylum,
## - constraint configuration,
## - and OvO binary submodels.
##
## This visualization helps identify microbial signatures
## that are stable, constraint-specific, or biologically
## relevant for CRC classification.
##
## ------------------------------------------------------------

p_top <- ggplot(alldf23, aes(x = model, y = species)) +
  
  geom_tile(
    aes(fill = importance),
    color = "grey90",
    linewidth = 0.3
  ) +
  
  geom_point(
    aes(color = coefficient),
    size = 3.8,
    stroke = 0,
    shape = 16,
    na.rm = TRUE
  ) +
  
  scale_fill_gradient(
    low = "white",
    high = "steelblue",
    name = "MDA | CV"
  ) +
  
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Sign",
    values = c(
      "firebrick1",
      "deepskyblue1",
      "white"
    ),
    breaks = c(-1, 1, 0),
    labels = c("-1", "1", ""),
    drop = TRUE
  ) +
  
  facet_grid(
    phylum ~ source,
    scales = "free_y",
    space = "free_y"
  ) +
  
  labs(
    title = "",
    x = NULL,
    y = NULL
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 20) +
  
  theme(
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      size = 16
    ),
    axis.text.y = element_text(size = 16),
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 10,
      r = 25,
      b = 10,
      l = 30
    ),
    strip.text.y = element_text(
      angle = 0,
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    legend.position = "right",
    legend.text = element_text(size = 16),
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 18,
      face = "bold"
    )
  )

print(p_top)
ggsave(
  filename = "~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/crc_heatmap.pdf",
  plot = p_top,
  device = "pdf",
  width = 16,
  height = 12
)
```





### The four files loaded below correspond to the experimental results obtained using our interpretable multiclass extension of Predomics applied to four gut microbiome datasets:

* **CRC**: colorectal cancer dataset;
* **T2D**: type 2 diabetes dataset;
* **Enterotype Balanced**: balanced enterotype dataset;
* **Enterotype Imbalanced**: imbalanced enterotype dataset.

For each experiment, we used:

* the **One-vs-One (OvO)** binarization strategy;
* an aggregation method based on **majority voting with tie-breaking**;
* the **semi-constrained** regime, which partially enforces feature-selection constraints in order to obtain more interpretable models while maintaining strong predictive performance.

These experiments were conducted as part of a comparative evaluation against several State-of-the-Art (SOTA) methods, including:

* **Random Forest (RF)**;
* **Logistic Regression (LR)**;
* **Support Vector Machine (SVM)**.

The loaded `.rda` files contain all results generated from the cross-validation experiments, including multiclass confusion matrices, performance metrics, OvO submodels, and all information required for the comparative analyses and visualizations presented in this study.



```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/res_clf_mc_CRC_2026.rda")
load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/res_clf_mc_T2D_2026.rda")
load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/res_clf_mc_balance_2026.rda")
load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/vignettes/res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026.rda")
```


```{r}
# =========================================================
# Build the four datasets
# =========================================================
df_crc <- get_aggregated_confusion_df(
  res_clf_mc_CRC_2026,
  "CRC"
)

df_t2d <- get_aggregated_confusion_df(
  res_clf_mc_T2D_2026,
  "T2D"
)

df_balance <- get_aggregated_confusion_df(
  res_clf_mc_balance_2026,
  "Enterotype Balanced"
)

df_imbalance <- get_aggregated_confusion_df(
  res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026,
  "Enterotype Imbalanced"
)

# =========================================================
# Merge all datasets
# =========================================================
df_all <- bind_rows(
  df_crc,
  df_t2d,
  df_balance,
  df_imbalance
)

df_all$Dataset <- factor(
  df_all$Dataset,
  levels = c(
    "CRC",
    "T2D",
    "Enterotype Balanced",
    "Enterotype Imbalanced"
  )
)

df_all$Facet_Label <- paste0(
  df_all$Dataset,
  "\n",
  df_all$Metrics
)

df_all$Facet_Label <- factor(
  df_all$Facet_Label,
  levels = unique(df_all$Facet_Label[order(df_all$Dataset)])
)

# =========================================================
# Text color according to cell intensity
# =========================================================
max_value <- max(df_all$Value, na.rm = TRUE)

df_all$Text_Color <- ifelse(
  df_all$Value > 0.45 * max_value,
  "white",
  "black"
)

# =========================================================
# Final merged plot
# =========================================================
p <- ggplot(df_all, aes(x = Predicted, y = Actual, fill = Value)) +
  
  geom_tile(color = "grey85", linewidth = 0.6) +
  
  geom_text(
    aes(label = Value, color = Text_Color),
    size = 5,
    fontface = "bold"
  ) +
  
  scale_color_identity() +
  
  scale_fill_gradientn(
    colours = c("#FFFFE5", "#C7E9B4", "#41B6C4", "#2C7FB8", "#081D58"),
    name = "Count"
  ) +
  
  facet_wrap(
    ~ Facet_Label,
    ncol = 2,
    scales = "free"
  ) +
  
  theme_minimal(base_size = 16) +
  
  labs(
    title = NULL,
    x = "Predicted class",
    y = "Actual class"
  ) +
  
  theme(
    strip.text = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold",
      lineheight = 1.15,
      margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 8, b = 12)
    ),
    
    axis.title.x = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      margin = ggplot2::margin(t = 20)
    ),
    
    axis.title.y = element_text(
      size = 20,
      face = "bold",
      margin = ggplot2::margin(r = 20)
    ),
    
    axis.text.x = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold",
      angle = 45,
      hjust = 1,
      vjust = 1
    ),
    
    axis.text.y = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    legend.title = element_text(
      size = 16,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    legend.text = element_text(
      size = 14,
      face = "bold"
    ),
    
    panel.spacing.x = grid::unit(3.2, "cm"),
    panel.spacing.y = grid::unit(2.8, "cm"),
    
    panel.grid = element_blank(),
    
    plot.margin = ggplot2::margin(
      t = 20,
      r = 35,
      b = 25,
      l = 35
    )
  )

print(p)

# =========================================================
# Save as PDF
# =========================================================
ggsave(
  filename = "confusion_matrices_4_datasets_cv10_article.pdf",
  plot = p,
  width = 22,
  height = 14,
  units = "in",
  dpi = 600
)
```



### Loading the best State-of-the-Art (SOTA) models

The files loaded below correspond to the best-performing State-of-the-Art (SOTA) multiclass classification models evaluated on the four gut microbiome datasets used in this study:

- **CRC** (Colorectal Cancer),
- **T2D** (Type 2 Diabetes),
- **Enterotype Balanced**,
- **Enterotype Imbalanced**.

These models were selected as the strongest baseline approaches for comparison with our interpretable multiclass Predomics framework.

The loaded experiments include the following SOTA methods:

- **Random Forest (RF)**,
- **Logistic Regression (LR)**,
- **Support Vector Machine (SVM)**.

All SOTA models were trained using the **One-vs-One (OvO)** multiclass decomposition strategy in order to ensure a fair and consistent comparison with the proposed Predomics multiclass extension.

The `.rda` files contain the complete experimental outputs generated during the cross-validation procedures, including:

- multiclass confusion matrices,
- prediction results,
- OvO submodels,
- performance metrics,
- and all information required for comparative analyses and visualization.

```{r}
load("~/Documents/multiclasse_predomics/mcpredomics/res_LOGIT_ovo_T2D_2026.rda")
```

```{r fig.width=16, fig.height=12, warning=FALSE}
# ======================================================
# Function: compute recall and precision from one binary matrix
# rows = Predicted, columns = Actual
# ======================================================

compute_metrics_one_binary_matrix_generic <- function(conf_mat, pair_classes, fold_id) {
  
  pair_classes <- as.character(pair_classes)
  pair_name <- paste(pair_classes, collapse = " vs ")
  
  aligned_mat <- matrix(
    0,
    nrow = length(pair_classes),
    ncol = length(pair_classes),
    dimnames = list(pair_classes, pair_classes)
  )
  
  valid_rows <- intersect(rownames(conf_mat), pair_classes)
  valid_cols <- intersect(colnames(conf_mat), pair_classes)
  
  aligned_mat[valid_rows, valid_cols] <- conf_mat[valid_rows, valid_cols, drop = FALSE]
  
  metrics_table <- data.frame()
  
  for (current_class in pair_classes) {
    
    TP <- aligned_mat[current_class, current_class]
    
    # rows = Predicted, columns = Actual
    FP <- sum(aligned_mat[current_class, ]) - TP
    FN <- sum(aligned_mat[, current_class]) - TP
    
    recall_value <- ifelse((TP + FN) == 0, NA, TP / (TP + FN))
    precision_value <- ifelse((TP + FP) == 0, NA, TP / (TP + FP))
    
    metrics_table <- rbind(
      metrics_table,
      data.frame(
        Fold = fold_id,
        Pair = pair_name,
        Class = current_class,
        Recall = recall_value,
        Precision = precision_value,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
  
  return(metrics_table)
}

# ======================================================
# Function: extract metrics for one method
# ======================================================

extract_crc_precision_recall <- function(result_object, method_name, class_order) {
  
  all_results_list <- list()
  result_index <- 1
  
  all_best_test_folds <- result_object$crossVal$best_fold_test
  
  if (!is.null(result_object$class_pairs)) {
    class_pairs <- result_object$class_pairs
  } else {
    class_pairs <- combn(class_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  }
  
  for (fold_index in seq_along(all_best_test_folds)) {
    
    current_fold <- all_best_test_folds[[fold_index]]
    
    if (!is.null(current_fold) && !is.null(current_fold$confusionMatrix_)) {
      
      binary_confusion_list <- current_fold$confusionMatrix_
      
      for (pair_index in seq_along(binary_confusion_list)) {
        
        current_binary_matrix <- binary_confusion_list[[pair_index]]
        
        if (!is.null(result_object$class_pairs)) {
          pair_classes <- class_pairs[[pair_index]]
        } else {
          pair_classes <- sort(unique(c(
            rownames(current_binary_matrix),
            colnames(current_binary_matrix)
          )))
        }
        
        all_results_list[[result_index]] <-
          compute_metrics_one_binary_matrix_generic(
            conf_mat = current_binary_matrix,
            pair_classes = pair_classes,
            fold_id = fold_index
          )
        
        result_index <- result_index + 1
      }
    }
  }
  
  all_metrics_df <- do.call(rbind, all_results_list)
  
  df_summary <- aggregate(
    cbind(Recall, Precision) ~ Pair + Class,
    data = all_metrics_df,
    FUN = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  df_plot <- melt(
    df_summary,
    id.vars = c("Pair", "Class"),
    measure.vars = c("Recall", "Precision"),
    variable.name = "Metric",
    value.name = "Score"
  )
  
  pair_order <- c(
    "adenoma vs control",
    "adenoma vs CRC",
    "control vs CRC"
  )
  
  df_plot$Pair <- factor(df_plot$Pair, levels = pair_order)
  df_plot$Class <- factor(df_plot$Class, levels = class_order)
  df_plot$Method <- method_name
  
  return(df_plot)
}

# ======================================================
# Plot function for one method
# ======================================================

make_crc_method_plot <- function(df_method, plot_title, show_legend = FALSE) {
  
  p <- ggplot(df_method, aes(x = Pair, y = Score, fill = Class)) +
    geom_bar(
      stat = "identity",
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      width = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = round(Score, 2)),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      vjust = -0.3,
      size = 4
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Metric, nrow = 1) +
    ylim(0, 1.08) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = NULL,
      y = "Score",
      fill = "Class"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(
        hjust = 0.5,
        face = "bold",
        size = 15
      ),
      axis.text.x = element_text(
        angle = 45,
        hjust = 1,
        face = "bold"
      ),
      strip.text = element_text(
        face = "bold",
        size = 13
      ),
      panel.border = element_rect(
        color = "black",
        fill = NA,
        linewidth = 0.7
      )
    )
  
  if (!show_legend) {
    p <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }
  
  return(p)
}
```

```{r fig.width=16, fig.heigth = 12}
  metrics_table <- data.frame()
  
  for (current_class in pair_classes) {
    
    TP <- aligned_mat[current_class, current_class]
    
    # rows = Predicted, columns = Actual
    FP <- sum(aligned_mat[current_class, ]) - TP
    FN <- sum(aligned_mat[, current_class]) - TP
    
    recall_value <- ifelse((TP + FN) == 0, NA, TP / (TP + FN))
    precision_value <- ifelse((TP + FP) == 0, NA, TP / (TP + FP))
    
    metrics_table <- rbind(
      metrics_table,
      data.frame(
        Fold = fold_id,
        Pair = pair_name,
        Class = current_class,
        Recall = recall_value,
        Precision = precision_value,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
  
  return(metrics_table)
}

extract_enterotype_balance_precision_recall <- function(result_object, method_name, class_order) {
  
  all_results_list <- list()
  result_index <- 1
  
  all_best_test_folds <- result_object$crossVal$best_fold_test
  
  if (!is.null(result_object$class_pairs)) {
    class_pairs <- result_object$class_pairs
  } else {
    class_pairs <- combn(class_order, 2, simplify = FALSE)
  }
  
  for (fold_index in seq_along(all_best_test_folds)) {
    
    current_fold <- all_best_test_folds[[fold_index]]
    
    if (!is.null(current_fold) && !is.null(current_fold$confusionMatrix_)) {
      
      binary_confusion_list <- current_fold$confusionMatrix_
      
      for (pair_index in seq_along(binary_confusion_list)) {
        
        current_binary_matrix <- binary_confusion_list[[pair_index]]
        
        if (!is.null(result_object$class_pairs)) {
          pair_classes <- class_pairs[[pair_index]]
        } else {
          pair_classes <- sort(unique(c(
            rownames(current_binary_matrix),
            colnames(current_binary_matrix)
          )))
        }
        
        all_results_list[[result_index]] <-
          compute_metrics_one_binary_matrix_generic(
            conf_mat = current_binary_matrix,
            pair_classes = pair_classes,
            fold_id = fold_index
          )
        
        result_index <- result_index + 1
      }
    }
  }
  
  all_metrics_df <- do.call(rbind, all_results_list)
  
  df_summary <- aggregate(
    cbind(Recall, Precision) ~ Pair + Class,
    data = all_metrics_df,
    FUN = function(x) mean(x, na.rm = TRUE)
  )
  
  df_plot <- melt(
    df_summary,
    id.vars = c("Pair", "Class"),
    measure.vars = c("Recall", "Precision"),
    variable.name = "Metric",
    value.name = "Score"
  )
  
  pair_order <- c(
    "Bact1 vs Bact2",
    "Bact1 vs Prev",
    "Bact1 vs Rum",
    "Bact2 vs Prev",
    "Bact2 vs Rum",
    "Prev vs Rum"
  )
  
  df_plot$Pair <- factor(df_plot$Pair, levels = pair_order)
  df_plot$Class <- factor(df_plot$Class, levels = class_order)
  df_plot$Method <- method_name
  
  return(df_plot)
}

enterotype_classes <- c("Bact1", "Bact2", "Prev", "Rum")

df_predomics_balance <- extract_enterotype_balance_precision_recall(
  result_object = res_clf_mc_balance_2026,
  method_name = "Predomics",
  class_order = enterotype_classes
)

df_rf_balance <- extract_enterotype_balance_precision_recall(
  result_object = res_RF_ovo_balance_2026,
  method_name = "Random Forest",
  class_order = enterotype_classes
)

df_svm_balance <- extract_enterotype_balance_precision_recall(
  result_object = res_SVM_ovo_balance_2026,
  method_name = "SVM",
  class_order = enterotype_classes
)

df_logit_balance <- extract_enterotype_balance_precision_recall(
  result_object = res_LOGIT_ovo_balance_2026,
  method_name = "Logistic Regression",
  class_order = enterotype_classes
)

make_enterotype_balance_method_plot <- function(df_method, plot_title, show_legend = FALSE) {
  
  p <- ggplot(df_method, aes(x = Pair, y = Score, fill = Class)) +
    geom_bar(
      stat = "identity",
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      width = 0.7
    ) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = round(Score, 2)),
      position = position_dodge(width = 0.8),
      vjust = -0.3,
      size = 3.5
    ) +
    facet_wrap(~ Metric, nrow = 1) +
    ylim(0, 1.08) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    labs(
      title = plot_title,
      x = NULL,
      y = "Score",
      fill = "Class"
    ) +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 15),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, face = "bold", size = 9),
      strip.text = element_text(face = "bold", size = 13),
      panel.border = element_rect(color = "black", fill = NA, linewidth = 0.7)
    )
  
  if (!show_legend) {
    p <- p + theme(legend.position = "none")
  }
  
  return(p)
}

p_predomics_balance <- make_enterotype_balance_method_plot(
  df_predomics_balance,
  plot_title = "Predomics",
  show_legend = FALSE
)

p_rf_balance <- make_enterotype_balance_method_plot(
  df_rf_balance,
  plot_title = "Random Forest",
  show_legend = TRUE
)

p_svm_balance <- make_enterotype_balance_method_plot(
  df_svm_balance,
  plot_title = "SVM",
  show_legend = FALSE
)

p_logit_balance <- make_enterotype_balance_method_plot(
  df_logit_balance,
  plot_title = "Logistic Regression",
  show_legend = TRUE
)

final_enterotype_balance_plot <-
  (p_predomics_balance | p_rf_balance) /
  (p_svm_balance | p_logit_balance) +
  plot_annotation(
    title = "Enterotype Balanced - Pairwise Class-Specific Recall and Precision",
    theme = theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 18)
    )
  )

ggsave(
  filename = "enterotype_balanced_precision_recall_per_class.pdf",
  plot = final_enterotype_balance_plot,
  width = 20,
  height = 11,
  dpi = 300
)

print(final_enterotype_balance_plot)
```

```{r}
# =========================================================
# AUROC and AUPRC computation for Predomics OvO submodels
# across 10-fold cross-validation for four datasets
# =========================================================

library(pROC)
library(PRROC)


# =========================================================
# 1. Compute AUROC and AUPRC for one binary classifier
# =========================================================
compute_binary_auc_metrics <- function(y_true, y_score) {
  
  keep_idx <- which(!is.na(y_true) & !is.na(y_score))
  y_true <- y_true[keep_idx]
  y_score <- y_score[keep_idx]
  
  if (length(unique(y_true)) < 2) {
    return(list(
      auroc = NA_real_,
      auprc = NA_real_
    ))
  }
  
  roc_obj <- pROC::roc(
    response = y_true,
    predictor = y_score,
    quiet = TRUE
  )
  
  auroc_value <- as.numeric(pROC::auc(roc_obj))
  
  scores_pos <- y_score[y_true == 1]
  scores_neg <- y_score[y_true == 0]
  
  pr_obj <- PRROC::pr.curve(
    scores.class0 = scores_pos,
    scores.class1 = scores_neg,
    curve = FALSE
  )
  
  auprc_value <- pr_obj$auc.integral
  
  return(list(
    auroc = auroc_value,
    auprc = auprc_value
  ))
}

# =========================================================
# 2. Extract the two classes of one OvO submodel
# =========================================================
get_ovo_classes_from_confmat <- function(confmat) {
  return(rownames(confmat))
}

# =========================================================
# 3. Compute AUROC and AUPRC for one fold
# =========================================================
compute_fold_binary_metrics <- function(res_object, fold_id, dataset_name) {
  
  fold_test <- res_object$crossVal$best_fold_test[[fold_id]]
  fold_xy <- res_object$crossVal$best_fold_xy[[fold_id]]
  
  confusion_list <- fold_test$confusionMatrix_
  scores_predictions <- fold_test$scores_predictions
  y_test_fold <- fold_xy$y_test
  
  n_submodels <- length(confusion_list)
  
  results <- data.frame(
    dataset = character(0),
    fold = integer(0),
    submodel = integer(0),
    class_pos = character(0),
    class_neg = character(0),
    n_samples = integer(0),
    auroc = numeric(0),
    auprc = numeric(0),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  
  for (k in seq_len(n_submodels)) {
    
    classes_k <- get_ovo_classes_from_confmat(
      confusion_list[[k]]
    )
    
    class_pos <- classes_k[1]
    class_neg <- classes_k[2]
    
    idx <- which(
      y_test_fold %in% c(class_pos, class_neg)
    )
    
    y_true <- ifelse(
      y_test_fold[idx] == class_pos,
      1,
      0
    )
    
    y_score <- scores_predictions[[k]][idx]
    
    if (length(y_score) != length(y_true)) {
      stop(
        paste0(
          "Length mismatch in ", dataset_name,
          " fold ", fold_id,
          ", submodel ", k,
          ": length(y_score) = ", length(y_score),
          ", length(y_true) = ", length(y_true)
        )
      )
    }
    
    met <- compute_binary_auc_metrics(
      y_true = y_true,
      y_score = y_score
    )
    
    results <- rbind(
      results,
      data.frame(
        dataset = dataset_name,
        fold = fold_id,
        submodel = k,
        class_pos = class_pos,
        class_neg = class_neg,
        n_samples = length(idx),
        auroc = met$auroc,
        auprc = met$auprc,
        stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
    )
  }
  
  return(results)
}

# =========================================================
# 4. Compute AUROC and AUPRC across all folds
# =========================================================
compute_all_folds_binary_metrics <- function(res_object, dataset_name) {
  
  n_folds <- length(res_object$crossVal$best_fold_test)
  all_results <- data.frame()
  
  for (fold_id in seq_len(n_folds)) {
    
    fold_results <- compute_fold_binary_metrics(
      res_object = res_object,
      fold_id = fold_id,
      dataset_name = dataset_name
    )
    
    all_results <- rbind(all_results, fold_results)
  }
  
  return(all_results)
}

# =========================================================
# 5. Summarize AUROC and AUPRC results
# =========================================================
summarize_binary_metrics <- function(all_results) {
  
  submodel_summary <- all_results %>%
    group_by(dataset, submodel, class_pos, class_neg) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_auroc = mean(auroc, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_auprc = mean(auprc, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  global_summary <- all_results %>%
    group_by(dataset) %>%
    summarise(
      mean_auroc = mean(auroc, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_auroc = sd(auroc, na.rm = TRUE),
      mean_auprc = mean(auprc, na.rm = TRUE),
      sd_auprc = sd(auprc, na.rm = TRUE),
      n_results = n(),
      .groups = "drop"
    )
  
  return(list(
    submodel_summary = submodel_summary,
    global_summary = global_summary
  ))
}

# =========================================================
# 6. Run analysis for the four Predomics datasets
# =========================================================
all_metrics_crc <- compute_all_folds_binary_metrics(
  res_object = res_clf_mc_CRC_2026,
  dataset_name = "CRC"
)

all_metrics_t2d <- compute_all_folds_binary_metrics(
  res_object = res_clf_mc_T2D_2026,
  dataset_name = "T2D"
)

all_metrics_balance <- compute_all_folds_binary_metrics(
  res_object = res_clf_mc_balance_2026,
  dataset_name = "Enterotype Balanced"
)

all_metrics_imbalance <- compute_all_folds_binary_metrics(
  res_object = res_clf_mc_imbalance_2026,
  dataset_name = "Enterotype Imbalanced"
)

# =========================================================
# 7. Merge all results
# =========================================================
all_metrics_predomics <- bind_rows(
  all_metrics_crc,
  all_metrics_t2d,
  all_metrics_balance,
  all_metrics_imbalance
)

# =========================================================
# 8. Summarize all results
# =========================================================
summary_metrics_predomics <- summarize_binary_metrics(
  all_metrics_predomics
)

cat("\n=== Mean AUROC/AUPRC by OvO submodel ===\n")
print(summary_metrics_predomics$submodel_summary)

cat("\n=== Global mean AUROC/AUPRC by dataset ===\n")
print(summary_metrics_predomics$global_summary)
# =========================================================
# Final article-ready table
# =========================================================
final_auc_table_predomics <- summary_metrics_predomics$global_summary %>%
  mutate(
    AUROC = paste0(round(mean_auroc, 3), " ± ", round(sd_auroc, 3)),
    AUPRC = paste0(round(mean_auprc, 3), " ± ", round(sd_auprc, 3))
  ) %>%
  select(dataset, AUROC, AUPRC)

print(final_auc_table_predomics)
```
